title: Best Virtual Assistant Companies in the Philippines 2026
summary: Find the right Philippines-based VA company with this November 2026 comparison of pricing, vetting, and co-management options.
body_markdown:
Most people searching for virtual assistant companies with Philippines-based assistants already know the Philippines is a great talent source. What’s less obvious is how much the service model behind your hire matters. Some companies co-manage your assistant after placement. Others place someone and leave the management to you. Picking the wrong one means you do a lot more work than you planned on.


**TLDR:**


- Some Philippines-based VA companies stay involved after placement (co-managed). Others place an assistant and leave the management to you.
- Among the companies compared here, MyOutDesk focuses on real estate, while BruntWork and Remote Leverage place an assistant and leave day-to-day management to you.
- Screening, contract flexibility, and 24/7 availability are the three factors that matter most when comparing VA companies.
- Magic hand-picks assistants, with Executive Assistants ($540/week) from the top 0.5% of applicants, co-manages them after placement, includes AI tools, and has no contract, starting at $360/week.


## What Are Virtual Assistant Companies With Philippines-Based Assistants?


[Virtual assistants](https://getmagic.com/blog/what-is-a-virtual-assistant/) from companies with Philippines-based staff are recruited, vetted, and placed by agencies or services to handle remote work from the Philippines to handle tasks for businesses and individuals, typically covering admin, customer support, scheduling, and research.


The Philippines has become the go-to source country for VA talent for a few concrete reasons:


- English is an official language, so communication rarely becomes a friction point.
- Filipino professionals are widely known for strong work ethic and adaptability to Western business norms.
- Wages are considerably lower than in the US or UK, giving businesses access to skilled help at a fraction of local hiring costs.
- Many Filipino VAs work schedules that overlap with US business hours or cover overnight gaps.


That said, how you access that talent matters as much as where it comes from. Freelance marketplaces let you hire directly, which keeps costs low but puts recruiting, onboarding, and management entirely on you. Managed VA agencies handle all of that, matching you with a vetted assistant, providing oversight, and stepping in if something goes wrong.


## How We Ranked These Virtual Assistant Companies


These rankings draw on publicly available information and reflect the criteria that actually matter to buyers. Picking a VA company without a clear framework is how you end up locked into a bad contract with an assistant who needed six weeks of training before they were useful.


Here’s what we looked at:


- Talent vetting rigor: How selective is the screening process, and does the company share specifics about acceptance rates or interview standards?
- Co-management and support: Does the company stay involved after placement, or does it hand you an assistant and disappear?
- Range of services: Can the company cover admin, customer support, sales, and[specialized types of virtual assistants](https://getmagic.com/blog/types-of-virtual-assistants/) , or is it limited to one or two task types?
- Pricing and contract flexibility: Are long-term commitments required, and is the cost structure transparent upfront?
- Availability and responsiveness: Can the assistant cover your hours, and is there backup coverage when needed?
- Consistency of assistant quality: Does the company have a track record of delivering reliable assistants beyond the first match?


Every assessment is based on publicly available information about each company’s model, pricing, and positioning.


## Best Overall Virtual Assistant Company: Magic


Magic launched in 2015 and hires assistants in the Philippines and Latin America. Magic picks the best assistant for each client, and its Executive Assistants come from the top 0.5% of applicants.


Here is what sets Magic apart from other virtual assistant companies:


- Candidates go through resume screening, an online assessment with an English test, a live video interview, and Magic’s live training, and only the top 0.5% of applicants make it as Executive Assistants
- Dedicated full-time assistants (40 hrs/week) are co-managed by Magic (see[how Magic works](https://getmagic.com/how-it-works/) ), so you’re never left to train or supervise alone
- VA[plans and pricing](https://getmagic.com/pricing/) start at $360/week; Executive Assistant plans start at $540/week, with no contract and cancel-anytime terms
- On Executive Assistant plans, Magic 24/7 on-demand concierge is available as backup whenever your dedicated assistant is offline
- Magic sets up and pays for a Claude account for every assistant and trains them on it, at no extra cost. Roles include executive, virtual, admin, customer support, and ecommerce assistants
- In business since 2015, with more than 10,000 businesses signed up and more than 1 million assistant applications received


Magic pairs serious vetting with co-managed ongoing support, flexible no-contract pricing, and round-the-clock availability on Executive Assistant plans, making it the strongest overall option on this list.


## MyOutDesk


MyOutDesk is one of several[virtual assistant companies](https://getmagic.com/blog/ranking-best-virtual-assistant-companies/) that places dedicated VAs, many from the Philippines, and it’s best known for its[real estate VA services](https://www.myoutdesk.com/industries/real-estate-virtual-assistants/) . The company says it has worked with 7,500+ real estate agents and brokers for more than 15 years.


### What They Offer


- Dedicated full-time VAs from the Philippines
- Real estate-specific roles: transaction coordination and lead generation
- Administrative, marketing, and customer service support
- Business process consulting alongside staffing


Good for real estate professionals who want a VA with transaction coordination or lead generation experience. MyOutDesk also lists healthcare, ecommerce, technology, finance, and insurance support, but its track record outside real estate is shorter.


## BruntWork


BruntWork is an offshore staffing company that sources remote workers primarily from the Philippines and other international markets. It operates closer to a recruitment and placement service than a[fully managed VA agency](https://getmagic.com/how-it-works/) .


That said, here is what they offer:


- Offshore VAs from the Philippines and a talent network in 60+ countries, covering customer support, admin, telesales, social media, and bookkeeping roles, per[BruntWork’s virtual assistant page](https://www.bruntwork.co/services/virtual-assistants/)
- Hourly rates of $4 to $8, no lock-in contracts, no setup fees, and staff from a minimum of 20 hours a week


Good for cost-focused businesses comfortable[hiring a virtual assistant](https://getmagic.com/blog/how-to-hire-a-virtual-assistant/) and managing their own remote workers day-to-day. BruntWork says its model gives clients full control over their operations. Clients direct and train their staff themselves. There is no ongoing oversight from a co-managed agency. For businesses that want an assistant who arrives ready to contribute, that gap matters.


## Remote Leverage


Remote Leverage is a VA recruiting agency that connects businesses with independent remote workers from the Philippines and Latin America. The model runs on a one-time placement fee instead of ongoing monthly charges.


### What They Offer


- VA recruiting from the Philippines and Latin America across admin, lead generation, sales, social media, and customer service roles
- An interview-before-hire process with no long-term contracts
- A one-time placement fee instead of recurring monthly costs


Good for budget-conscious entrepreneurs who want to self-manage an independent VA. That said, once the hire is made, day-to-day management is yours, with a Customer Success Manager for support but no backup coverage. For businesses that need a dependable assistant long-term without taking on a part-time HR role, that’s a steep ask.


## Wing Assistant


[Wing Assistant](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/wingassistant.com) is a managed VA service. Its[service tiers page](https://wingassistant.com/advanced-tiers/) says every plan includes a dedicated assistant, a Customer Success Manager, QA oversight, and backup coverage.


### What They Offer


- Entry-tier plans start at $699/month part-time and $999/month full-time, with higher tiers for more experienced assistants
- A 24/7 after-hours add-on starts at $149/month
- Roles across executive, personal, real estate, healthcare, and ecommerce assistants, plus customer service
- Bilingual English/Spanish sales callers


Good for small businesses that want part-time managed help at a lower monthly price. Worth checking[how much a virtual assistant costs](https://getmagic.com/blog/how-much-is-a-virtual-assistant/) before deciding. Round-the-clock coverage costs extra, because 24/7 after-hours help is a paid add-on.

Most VA services make you choose between affordability and accountability. Magic doesn’t ask you to. You get an assistant from the top 0.5% of applicants, co-managed by Magic after placement, backed by 24/7 on-demand coverage, and available across admin, sales, customer support, and specialized roles, all on a no-contract basis at $540/week on an Executive Assistant plan.


For anyone serious about[finding the best virtual assistant](https://getmagic.com/blog/best-virtual-assistant/) without taking on the recruiting, training, and oversight burden yourself, Magic is the most complete option on this list.


## Final Thoughts on Comparing Virtual Assistant Companies With Philippines-Based Assistants


The right VA company depends on how much you want to manage after the hire is made. Some services hand you a worker and step back, others stay in the picture and keep things running. Knowing which model fits your business makes the whole search a lot shorter.


**How do I choose the right virtual assistant company with Philippines-based assistants for my business?**


Start by deciding how much management responsibility you want to take on. If you want a ready-to-go assistant with ongoing oversight built in, co-managed agencies like Magic or Wing Assistant are the stronger fit. If you’re comfortable handling onboarding and day-to-day direction yourself, placement-only services like BruntWork or Remote Leverage keep costs lower.


**Is Magic a better fit than Wing Assistant for businesses that need round-the-clock coverage?**


Yes. Wing Assistant offers part-time and full-time plans starting at $699/month with backup coverage, but 24/7 after-hours help is a paid add-on. Magic’s Executive Assistant plans come paired with Magic 24/7 on-demand concierge, so you have coverage even when your primary assistant is offline, which matters most for time-sensitive or high-volume operations.


**When should I consider MyOutDesk over the other virtual assistant companies on this list?**


MyOutDesk makes the most sense if you work specifically in real estate and need a VA with genuine experience in transaction coordination or lead generation. For any other industry, its talent pool skews too narrowly to compete with options like Magic that cover admin, sales, ecommerce, customer support, and more.


**What is the difference between a co-managed VA agency and a placement-only service?**


A co-managed agency like Magic stays involved after your assistant is placed, providing performance coaching and oversight, plus backup support on Executive Assistant plans. A placement-only service like Remote Leverage or BruntWork handles recruiting, then hands the hire over to you, leaving onboarding, training, and daily management on your plate.


**Can a small business or solopreneur realistically afford a Philippines-based virtual assistant from one of these companies?**


Yes. Wing Assistant’s part-time plans start at $699/month. Magic’s VA plans start at $360/week with no long-term contract, which is still considerably less than a local in-house hire. Remote Leverage’s one-time placement fee is worth considering if you want to self-manage and avoid recurring agency costs altogether.


**What tasks can a Philippines-based virtual assistant realistically handle from day one?**


A well-vetted Philippines-based VA can handle email management, calendar scheduling, customer support, data entry, research, and social media tasks from the start. With a co-managed agency like Magic, assistants arrive already trained and coached, so the ramp-up period is much shorter than hiring independently through a freelance marketplace.


**How do I know if a virtual assistant company is actually vetting candidates or just posting job boards?**


Look for agencies that share specific acceptance rates, describe their interview process in detail, and assign a human to match you with your assistant. Magic, for example, selects only the top 0.5% of applicants as Executive Assistants, with hand-picked matching by a person rather than an algorithm.


**Magic vs BruntWork: which one is better if I want someone to manage my assistant for me?**


Magic is the stronger choice if you want co-management built in. BruntWork handles recruitment and placement, but once the hire is made, onboarding, training, and daily oversight are your responsibility. Magic stays involved after placement with ongoing performance coaching, plus backup coverage on Executive Assistant plans.


**What happens if my dedicated Philippines-based assistant is sick or unavailable?**


With a Magic Executive Assistant plan, your assistant is backed by Magic 24/7 on-demand concierge, so coverage continues even when your primary assistant is offline.


**How quickly can I get a Philippines-based virtual assistant up and running?**


With a managed agency like Magic, you can have a vetted, matched assistant ready to start in under a week. Freelance marketplaces can move faster on paper, but the time you spend recruiting, interviewing, and onboarding yourself often pushes the real start date much further out.


**Remote Leverage vs Magic: which is better for someone who wants to self-manage their VA?**


Remote Leverage suits self-managers well since its one-time placement fee keeps ongoing costs low and you retain full control of day-to-day direction. Magic is the better fit if you want co-management and ongoing coaching, plus backup coverage on Executive Assistant plans, and are willing to pay a recurring weekly rate for that support structure.


**What is Magic 24/7 and how does it work alongside a dedicated assistant?**


Magic 24/7, included with Executive Assistant plans, is an on-demand concierge service available around the clock for urgent tasks or to fill gaps when your dedicated assistant is offline. It works as a built-in safety net rather than a replacement, so you always have someone available without hiring a second assistant.


**How do AI tools factor into what Philippines-based virtual assistants can do for my business?**


AI tools help assistants work faster and handle more complex research, drafting, and data tasks without sacrificing accuracy.


**What specialized roles can Philippines-based VA companies fill beyond general admin support?**


Depending on the agency, Philippines-based VAs can cover customer support, ecommerce management, sales, bookkeeping, HR support, and even real estate transaction coordination. Magic supports the broadest range of specialized roles across industries, while options like MyOutDesk lean heavily toward real estate.


**Is there a long-term contract required when hiring through most virtual assistant companies with Philippines-based assistants?**


Contract requirements vary by company. Magic operates on a no-contract, cancel-anytime basis with payment starting only after you select your assistant. Remote Leverage and BruntWork also avoid long-term commitments, while some agencies have not made their contract terms publicly clear.
